item.title: Holographic Quantum Transformer: A Generalist Neuro-Symbolic Architecture for Solving Frustrated Systems via Generative Attention
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Xingran Guo, Tiaojie Xiao, Jie Liu, Keqin Li
arXiv:2607.00398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating two-dimensional frustrated quantum matter is a grand challenge due to the sign problem and exponential Hilbert space complexity. In this work, we introduce the Holographic Quantum Transformer (HQT), a physics-inspired generative architecture that leverages global self-attention to resolve non-local entanglement patterns. We validate HQT on the square lattice J₁₋J₂ Heisenberg model. On the heavily frustrated 8 × 8 lattice at the quantum critical point (J₂₌₀.5), HQT reaches a ground-state energy per site (E/N) of -0.5001(1), consistent with the expected finite-size scaling trend. Beyond numerical accuracy, HQT exhibits intrinsic physical awareness, autonomously recovering the underlying J₂ interaction geometry through interpretable…

item.title: A dual machine learning framework for the solution of the inverse scattering problem in cylindrical plasmas
item.description:
📚 Machine Learning: Science and Technology
👤 Christos Vagkidis, Ewout Devlaminck, Mirko Ramisch, Günter E M Tovar and Alf Köhn-Seemann
Machine learning algorithms are widely used to replace or accelerate high-fidelity codes and to provide physical insight in complex problems. In this work, a random forest is applied to replace a 3D full-wave simulation performed using the COMSOL Multiphysics software. In our simulation, a microwave beam is propagating through a cylindrically shaped plasma and is scattered by it. The training data of the random forest consist of the electron density profiles and the corresponding distributions of the microwave beam power after the interaction with the plasma. The random forest accurately reproduces the resulting scattered beam distribution for a given density profile. A synthetic dataset is then created with the forest, which in turn is used to train a neural network (NN). The NN is train…

item.title: Automatic charge state tuning of 300 mm silicon quantum dots using neural network segmentation of charge stability diagram
item.description:
📚 Machine Learning: Science and Technology
👤 Peter Samaha, Amine Torki, Ysaline Renaud, Sam Fiette, Emmanuel Chanrion, Pierre-André Mortemousque and Yann Beilliard
Tuning of gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) is a major bottleneck for scaling spin-qubit technologies. We present a deep learning driven, semantic-segmentation pipeline that performs charge auto-tuning by locating transition lines in full charge stability diagrams (CSDs) and returns gate voltage targets for the single charge regime. We assemble and manually annotate a large, heterogeneous dataset of 1015 experimental CSDs measured from fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) QD devices, spanning nine design geometries, multiple wafers, and fabrication runs. A U-Net style convolutional neural network with a MobileNetV2 encoder is trained and validated through five-fold group cross-validation. Our model achieves an overall offline tuning success of 80.0% in locating the sin…

item.title: Machine learning framework for GW calculations across molecular dynamics trajectories
item.description:
📚 Machine Learning: Science and Technology
👤 Ragab A Abdelghany, Chih-En Hsu, Hung-Chung Hsueh, Yuan-Hong Tsai and Ming-Chiang Chung
Machine learning offers a transformative approach to overcoming the computational bottlenecks of quasiparticle energy calculations in many-body perturbation theory. While the approximation provides a rigorous description of excited-state electronic properties, its high computational cost—driven by the evaluation of the inverse dielectric matrix—renders it prohibitive for molecular dynamics (MD) simulations that require sampling thousands of thermal configurations. We present a gradient-boosting framework (LightGBM) that predicts quasiparticle energies with high efficiency using only computationally inexpensive mean-field density functional theory eigenvalues and exchange-correlation potentials. Trained on a minimal subset (25%) of MD snapshots for silicon and boron nitride, the model achi…

arXiv:2607.01197v2 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computing has emerged as a promising computational paradigm for machine learning (ML), with the potential to offer computational advantages over classical approaches. At this stage, the evidence supporting the performance and advantages of quantum machine learning (QML) models relative to classical models is insufficient. To address this gap, this paper presents an empirical study on the performance of QML models and their classical counterparts. We compare seven model pairs spanning supervised learning and reinforcement learning. Our results indicate that the evaluated quantum machine learning models do not yet surpass the classical baselines in overall prediction performance, policy stability, or training time. arXiv:2607.00739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence with physical modeling offers a transformative route for accelerating the design of active nanophotonic devices. Using high-index metasurfaces cavity, the NanoPhotoNet-Lase model iden…

arXiv:2607.00301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergence of powerful deep generative models based on diffusion and flow matching has enabled the learning and modeling of complex distributions. By converting density matrix into the spin Wigner function and leveraging functional flow matching to learn distributions in function space, QFM enables accurate and effective learning of multi-qubit quantum distributions. item.title: Near-Sensor Damage Localization in Multi-Story Buildings with Level-Crossing Spike Encoding and a Compact Spiking Neural Network
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Saher Elsayed, Mohamed Ali, Khairi Azhar Aziz
Wireless, battery-powered accelerometer nodes are widely used for vibration-based structural health monitoring (SHM), but battery life limits the energy for sampling, on-node inference, and radio transmission. We ask whether an event-driven spike front-end can localize stiffness-degrading damage in a multi-story building while making compute cost scale with signal content. Our pipeline places a small modal filterbank before a level-crossing (temporal-contrast) encoder whose single threshold ((θ)) jointly controls accuracy, synaptic-operation count, and the data volume leaving the sensor; a tiny feed-forward spiking neural network (SNN) trained with a surrogate gradient then classifies the spikes. On a six-class task for a five-story shear building under ambient excitation with random dama…

item.title: 基于深度神经网络、实时图映射与性能分析的无线传感器网络节点级故障监测
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Manjunatha A S, Dr. Venkatramana Bhat P, Dr. Ramakrishna M
该研究提出一种用于无线传感器网络节点级故障识别的深度学习方法，利用温度、电池寿命和传感器读数等时间特征进行建模。研究比较了 CNN、RNN 和 LSTM 模型在故障节点分类中的表现，并使用准确率、精确率、召回率、F1 值和混淆矩阵进行评估。结果通过实时图映射界面动态展示节点状态，以提高故障监测的可解释性和实用性。

item.title: 基于稀疏回归与神经网络的近壁球体降阶水动力建模
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Zev Hoffman, Sara Vahaji, Arpan Das, Micheal Candon, Daniel Sgarioto, Jayarathne Nirman, Pier Marzocca
本文提出一种可解释的参数化替代模型，用于实时预测物体轨迹中的水动力效应，研究对象为靠近垂直壁面、具有单自由度升沉运动的球体。作者利用高保真 CFD 生成不同壁距和下落高度下的升沉衰减响应数据，并对每条轨迹应用 SINDy 识别低阶非线性常微分方程，刻画等效静水恢复力、辐射阻尼和波浪激励。随后将 SINDy 得到的系数作为先验约束嵌入神经算子网络，使其学习输入参数到 ODE 系数的平滑映射，从而无需重复昂贵 CFD 即可预测任意参数点的动力学。

arXiv:2607.00506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnets provide a promising platform for spin-polarized transport without net magnetization, but their transport properties are usually discussed in terms of momentum-space spin splitting. Here, using first-principles calculations and quantum transport simulations, we show that the charge-ordered altermagnet α-Fe₂PO₅ exhibits a distinct form of real-space spin selectivity despite weak altermagnetic spin splitting near the Fermi level. The charge order creates inequivalent Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺ sites within each sublattice, while the puckered C-type antiferromagnetic stacking suppresses inter-sublattice transport. item.description:

👤 Zefei Han, Haojin Wang, Yuanchang Li
arXiv:2510.22636v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Much is known about the magnetoelectric effect of multiferroic insulators, yet little is understood about multiferroic metals. In this work, we propose a stacking engineering strategy based on monolayer magnets to construct multiferroic metals, with validation through first-principles calculations on six experimentally synthesized materials. Such multiferroic metals exhibit predominantly linear magnetoelectric response, originating from direct spin-charge interactions as a result of external field-modulated Fermi energy. This fundamentally differs from spin-charge-lattice or spin-orbit coupling mechanisms in multiferroic insulators, offering application advantages in the field of high-speed response. arXiv:2602.12223v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the edge state properties of a two-dimensional kagome lattice using a tight-binding approach, focusing on the role of lattice termination, spin-orbit coupling, and magnetic order. In the pristine limit, we show that the existence of localized edge states is highly sensitive to boundary geometry, with certain terminations completely suppressing edge modes. Kane-Mele spin-orbit coupling opens a bulk gap and stabilizes topologically protected helical edge states, yielding a robust Z₂ insulating phase that is insensitive to termination details. arXiv:2607.00993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnets, distinguished by compensated antiparallel spins yet nondegenerate magnon spectra, bridge the gap between ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. 👤 Chuang Chen, Subir Sachdev, Zi Yang Meng
arXiv:2607.00762v2 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal d-wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. 👤 Zhuo-Cheng Gu, Hiroaki Ishizuka
arXiv:2607.00807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling magnetism by electric field or current is a central topic in spintronics. In this work, we argue that the magnon spin photocurrent can also be controlled by the electric field in magnetoelectrics. Taking Cr₂O₃ as an example, we demonstrate how the spin current is modified by the electric field, using nonlinear response theory. We find that the Dzyaloshinsky--Moriya interaction induced by the applied field plays a key role in modifying spin-current conductivity, which exhibits pronounced anisotropy with respect to the light polarization. item.title: 金属 Kagome 反铁磁体 CrRhAs 的磁性质与电输运性质
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Franziska Breitner, Bin Shen, Anton Jesche, Alexander A. Tsirlin, Philipp Gegenwart
该研究报道了反铁磁 Kagome 金属 CrRhAs 单晶的合成与基础表征，该材料被预测具有带矢量自旋手征性的非平庸自旋纹理。电输运、热容和磁化测量显示其在约 150 K 发生反铁磁转变。Hall 电阻率随磁场线性变化，未观察到非线性 Hall 贡献；但不同电流和磁场构型下 Hall 系数发生符号变化，并在面内电流构型的 Néel 温度以下显著增强，提示费米面重构或磁振子散射的作用。

item.title: Haldane-Hubbard模型中奇宇称交替磁性诱导的陈绝缘相重构
item.description:

该研究利用团簇从旋自旋方法表明，Haldane-Hubbard模型的交替磁性陈绝缘相中出现的奇宇称交替磁性，会显著重构传统陈绝缘相的局域拓扑结构，但总陈数保持不变。其结果包括贝里曲率的自旋与谷选择性、锯齿边界中手征对称性破缺边缘态的出现，以及扶手椅边界反演对称性的保持。光学响应显示局域重构与全局拓扑相分离：低能谱由能隙附近准粒子主导，而低频霍尔电导仍保持量子化。

item.title: 基于磁性 Fe3O4/CoFe2O4/Ce-BDC 杂化纳米酶的硫化物双模式比色与 RGB 检测
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Qingyuan Weng, Xinyi Wen, Tianyuan Wei, Qing Zhang, Wanying Zhu, Junli Hong
该研究构建了一种用于硫化物检测的双模式传感策略，将磁性 Fe3O4/CoFe2O4/Ce-BDC 纳米酶与 TMB/H2O2 显色体系结合。该纳米酶具有类过氧化物酶活性，可催化 TMB 氧化生成蓝色产物；硫化物在酸性条件下清除活性氧并还原氧化态 TMB，使 651 nm 吸光度降低并产生由蓝到无色的可视变化。该方法可通过分光光度法和智能手机 RGB 比色实现定量检测，检测限分别为 0.29 µM 和 31.26 µM。

item.title: Bridging Quantum Computing Paradigms toward Semiconductor Yield: A Controlled CV-versus-DV Comparison on Wafer-Map Defect Classification
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Yeonhong Kim, Jonghyeok Im, Monu Nath Baitha, Kyoungsik Kim
